sentences.en: It's been 50 years since the U.S.
sentences.zh: 距离美国卫生局局长发布关于吸烟与健康的报告已经过去50年了，

sentences.en: Surgeon General's report on smoking and health spurred one of the largest public health behavior change success stories of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 该报告推动了20世纪最成功的公共卫生行为改变案例之一。

sentences.en: Before and since this groundbreaking report's release, psychology has been at the forefront of smoking cessation efforts.
sentences.zh: 在这份开创性报告发布前后，心理学一直处于戒烟工作的最前沿。

sentences.en: Research into the biological and behavioral mechanisms of addiction has led to many successful treatments for nicotine addicts.
sentences.zh: 对成瘾的生物学和行为机制的研究，已经为尼古丁成瘾者带来了许多成功的治疗方法。

sentences.en: In this episode, we talk with Dr. Sherry McKee, a researcher whose work has focused on gender differences in smoking.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们采访了雪莉·麦基博士，她是一位专注于研究吸烟性别差异的研究员。

sentences.en: She discusses why women have a harder time kicking the habit and what science can do to help them quit.
sentences.zh: 她探讨了为什么女性更难戒掉烟瘾，以及科学能做些什么来帮助她们戒烟。

sentences.en: Sherry McKee has been working on finding out why women have a harder time quitting smoking than men.
sentences.zh: 雪莉·麦基一直致力于找出为什么女性比男性更难戒烟的原因。

sentences.en: Her work focuses on the roles stress and depression play in smoking behaviors for both men and women.
sentences.zh: 她的工作重点是压力和抑郁在男女吸烟行为中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: She is director of the Yale Behavioral Pharmacology Laboratory.
sentences.zh: 她是耶鲁大学行为药理学实验室的主任。

sentences.en: She's also an associate professor of psychiatry at the Yale School of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 她同时也是耶鲁大学医学院的精神病学副教授。

sentences.en: Her smoking research has been funded by the Office of Research on Women's Health and the National Institute of Drug Abuse.
sentences.zh: 她的吸烟研究得到了女性健康研究办公室和国家药物滥用研究所的资助。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. McKee.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，麦基博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: Is there a critical health disparity among female smokers?
sentences.zh: 女性吸烟者之间是否存在严重的健康差异？

sentences.en: And if so, what is being done to address that?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，目前正在采取什么措施来解决这个问题？

sentences.en: There are critical health disparities among women smokers.
sentences.zh: 女性吸烟者之间确实存在严重的健康差异。

sentences.en: Smoking is still the leading cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 吸烟仍然是美国导致可预防性疾病和死亡的首要原因。

sentences.en: Obesity is second.
sentences.zh: 肥胖排在第二位。

sentences.en: Alcohol use is third.
sentences.zh: 饮酒排在第三位。

sentences.en: We know that across industrialized nations, women smokers are going to be responsible for a half million deaths per year,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在工业化国家，女性吸烟者每年将导致50万人死亡，

sentences.en: and this rate is expected to exponentially increase over the next 25 years.
sentences.zh: 而且这个比例预计在未来25年内会呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: Now, with regards to their health effects, when you equate tobacco exposure between men and women, women are more susceptible to serious tobacco-related disease,
sentences.zh: 现在，关于健康影响方面，当你在男女之间进行烟草暴露量对比时，女性更容易受到严重的烟草相关疾病的影响，

sentences.en: and this includes things like lung cancer and heart disease.
sentences.zh: 这包括肺癌和心脏病等疾病。

sentences.en: Women also experience sex-specific health risks, primarily related to their reproductive health.
sentences.zh: 女性还会经历性别特有的健康风险，主要与她们的生殖健康有关。

sentences.en: So they have problems with their menstrual cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以她们会有月经周期方面的问题。

sentences.en: They enter menopause earlier.
sentences.zh: 她们进入更年期的时间更早。

sentences.en: And, of course, women who smoke during pregnancy have a whole host of pregnancy-related negative or adverse events, things like preeclampsia and then lower birth weight babies.
sentences.zh: 当然，怀孕期间吸烟的女性会面临一系列与怀孕相关的负面或不良事件，比如先兆子痫，以及婴儿出生体重较低等问题。

sentences.en: So in addition to women experiencing more health-related effects of smoking, women are also less able to quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了女性会经历更多与吸烟相关的健康影响外，女性戒烟的能力也较弱。

sentences.en: There's been national data that's being collected over the last 40 years, and every single year for the last 40 years, quit rates for women are lower than quit rates for men.
sentences.zh: 过去40年里收集的全国数据显示，在过去的40年里，女性的戒烟率每年都低于男性。

sentences.en: Now, compounding this problem, currently available medications are not as effective, or generally not as effective, for women smokers.
sentences.zh: 现在，加剧这个问题的是，目前可用的药物对女性吸烟者来说效果并不那么好，或者说通常效果不佳。

sentences.en: To some extent, all of these medications, which are approved by the FDA, all target the nicotinic receptor in the brain, and this might not be the optimal strategy for women.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，所有这些获得美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准的药物，都是针对大脑中的尼古丁受体，但这可能不是女性的最佳策略。

sentences.en: So it's interesting to learn that women have more difficulty quitting smoking than men.
sentences.zh: 所以了解到女性比男性更难戒烟，这很有意思。

sentences.en: You know, given that the CDC has said women tend to be more health-conscious than men, you know, you would think that quitting smoking would maybe be easier,
sentences.zh: 你知道，鉴于美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）曾表示女性往往比男性更有健康意识，你会认为戒烟可能更容易，

sentences.en: but can you tell us what you've learned about why this is not the case?
sentences.zh: 但你能告诉我们你所了解到的为什么事实并非如此吗？

sentences.en: Well, there have been a number of factors identified that are thought to underlie why women have more difficulty quitting smoking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，已经确定了许多被认为导致女性更难戒烟的因素。

sentences.en: These include things like factors related to their menstrual cycle, also smoking to manage their weight, and smoking to regulate their negative mood and stress.
sentences.zh: 这些因素包括与月经周期相关的因素，还有为了控制体重而吸烟，以及为了调节负面情绪和压力而吸烟。

sentences.en: Part of your work focuses on tailoring treatments for women who are trying to quit, and why do you think gender-specific treatments can work, and could you provide an example?
sentences.zh: 你的部分工作专注于为试图戒烟的女性量身定制治疗方案，你认为性别特异性治疗为什么有效？你能提供一个例子吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: To develop effective treatments for women smokers, we need to target factors which underlie their smoking behavior.
sentences.zh: 为了开发针对女性吸烟者的有效治疗方法，我们需要针对导致她们吸烟行为的因素。

sentences.en: Now, this is a bit of a generalization, but across a number of studies, we know that women generally smoke to regulate negative mood and stress, more so than men.
sentences.zh: 这虽然有点概括化，但通过多项研究，我们知道女性通常比男性更倾向于通过吸烟来调节负面情绪和压力。

sentences.en: That's not to say that men don't smoke when they're stressed, but this is more true for women than it is for men.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说男性在有压力时不吸烟，但这对于女性来说比男性更适用。

sentences.en: And when you look at men, they tend to smoke more for the reinforcement that they receive from nicotine.
sentences.zh: 当你观察男性时，他们往往更多地为了从尼古丁中获得的强化作用而吸烟。

sentences.en: And again, this is not to say that women don't also receive reinforcement for nicotine, but it's not as strong as a factor that motivates their smoking as it is for men.
sentences.zh: 同样，这并不是说女性不会从尼古丁中获得强化，但这并不是像对男性那样，成为激励她们吸烟的强烈因素。

sentences.en: So we are currently targeting what's called the norgeneric system in the brain to understand if this is an important focus for developing medications to treat smokers.
sentences.zh: 所以我们目前正在针对大脑中所谓的去甲肾上腺素系统进行研究，以了解这是否是开发治疗吸烟者药物的一个重要焦点。

sentences.en: From animal studies, we know that this system is involved in stress responses, and it's also involved in the reinforcement from nicotine.
sentences.zh: 从动物研究中，我们知道这个系统参与了压力反应，也参与了尼古丁的强化作用。

sentences.en: We feel that medications targeting this system may be effective for both women and men, but might operate through different mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 我们认为针对该系统的药物可能对女性和男性都有效，但可能通过不同的机制发挥作用。

sentences.en: And our initial studies have shown this to be the case.
sentences.zh: 我们的初步研究已经证明了这一点。

sentences.en: We've studied a medication called guanfacine, which was originally developed as a blood pressure medication.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了一种名为胍法辛的药物，它最初是作为一种降压药开发的。

sentences.en: In smokers, we have shown that it decreases smoking in men and women, but that it tends to reduce the effect of stress
sentences.zh: 在吸烟者中，我们已经证明它能减少男性和女性的吸烟量，但它往往能减轻压力的影响，

sentences.en: and the negative effect that stress has on smoking behavior, more so for women.
sentences.zh: 以及压力对吸烟行为的负面影响，这对女性来说更为明显。

sentences.en: And then it also tends to reduce nicotine-related reinforcement, more so for men.
sentences.zh: 同时，它也往往能减少与尼古丁相关的强化作用，这对男性来说更为明显。

sentences.en: We are excited by the potential of this research to improve quit rates for both women and men.
sentences.zh: 我们对这项研究在提高男女戒烟率方面的潜力感到兴奋。

sentences.en: So you're talking a lot about how stress relates to smoking.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈了很多关于压力与吸烟的关系。

sentences.en: What do we know about how stress impacts smokers and their ability to quit?
sentences.zh: 关于压力如何影响吸烟者及其戒烟能力，我们了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Stress is a primary reason why people continue to smoke, and also it's a primary reason why people relapse back to smoking.
sentences.zh: 压力是人们持续吸烟的主要原因，也是人们复吸的主要原因。

sentences.en: Most smokers want to quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 大多数吸烟者都想戒烟。

sentences.en: If you ask a smoker, you know, if they want to quit, they'll say yes, and then you ask them about their current plans to quit, and they'll say, well, now's not a good time.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个吸烟者他们是否想戒烟，他们会说是，然后你问他们目前的戒烟计划，他们会说，现在不是好时机。

sentences.en: I have a big deadline at work.
sentences.zh: 我在工作中有个大限期。

sentences.en: My kids are really stressing me out.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们让我压力很大。

sentences.en: They'll identify some barriers that prevent them from engaging in a quit attempt, and very often they're stress-related.
sentences.zh: 他们会指出一些阻碍他们尝试戒烟的障碍，而这些障碍通常与压力有关。

sentences.en: We know that stress has a larger effect on women smoking than men.
sentences.zh: 我们知道压力对女性吸烟的影响比对男性更大。

sentences.en: We've conducted a number of laboratory studies where we bring men and women into the lab.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一些实验室研究，将男性和女性带入实验室。

sentences.en: We stress them out, and we find that women reach for cigarettes much more quickly than men, and they smoke them much more intensely when they're stressed.
sentences.zh: 我们给他们施加压力，发现女性在压力下比男性更快地去拿香烟，而且吸得更猛烈。

sentences.en: So they inhale more deeply, and they also take more puffs from a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 所以她们吸得更深，而且抽一支烟吸的口数也更多。

sentences.en: What about depression and smoking?
sentences.zh: 那么抑郁症和吸烟呢？

sentences.en: How prevalent is smoking among people with depression, and what's being done to help clinically depressed people who are addicted to cigarettes?
sentences.zh: 抑郁症患者中吸烟的普遍程度如何？对于那些对香烟上瘾的临床抑郁症患者，目前有什么帮助措施？

sentences.en: Right now in the U.S., about 8% meet criteria for major depression, and about 40% of these people smoke, so it's a huge number.
sentences.zh: 目前在美国，约有8%的人符合重度抑郁症的标准，其中约40%的人吸烟，所以这是一个巨大的数字。

sentences.en: This is double the rate of smoking among U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是美国成年人吸烟率的两倍，

sentences.en: adults, which is currently at about 20%.
sentences.zh: 目前约为20%。

sentences.en: We know that individuals with depression have more difficulty quitting, yet very little is known about how best to help them stop smoking.
sentences.zh: 我们知道抑郁症患者更难戒烟，但关于如何最好地帮助他们戒烟，我们知之甚少。

sentences.en: We've conducted a review of the research that's been conducted, and we found that most smokers that are studied have lifetime diagnosis of depression versus,
sentences.zh: 我们对已有的研究进行了回顾，发现大多数被研究的吸烟者都有终身抑郁症诊断，而不是，

sentences.en: so they had depression at some point in their past versus being currently depressed.
sentences.zh: 也就是说他们过去某个时候患有抑郁症，而不是目前正处于抑郁状态。

sentences.en: So those that are currently depressed have not been a huge focus of the research.
sentences.zh: 所以那些目前患有抑郁症的人并不是研究的重点。

sentences.en: Additionally, most studies will exclude, even if they're studying depressed smokers, they'll exclude people who are currently taking a medication or an antidepressant
sentences.zh: 此外，大多数研究会排除，即使是在研究抑郁的吸烟者时，也会排除那些目前正在服用药物或抗抑郁药的人，

sentences.en: to help treat their depression.
sentences.zh: 以帮助治疗他们的抑郁症。

sentences.en: We know that depression seems to have a greater negative impact on women and their ability to quit smoking across a few of these studies,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在几项研究中，抑郁症似乎对女性及其戒烟能力产生了更大的负面影响，

sentences.en: yet the studies, or the majority of studies, do not focus on comparing men and women.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些研究，或者说大多数研究，并没有专注于比较男性和女性。

sentences.en: There are some studies which suggest that adding a component to help people manage their mood states can be effective and can help improve rates of people being able to quit.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明，增加一个帮助人们管理情绪状态的环节是有效的，并且可以帮助提高人们的戒烟率。

sentences.en: But we know that smokers with depression have more severe tobacco withdrawal symptoms, experience more craving, and these factors could be targets of future treatment development.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，患有抑郁症的吸烟者有更严重的戒断症状，经历更强烈的渴望，这些因素可能成为未来治疗发展的目标。

sentences.en: Talking about nicotine, and you mentioned stress and depression, you know, obviously nicotine plays a role.
sentences.zh: 谈到尼古丁，你提到了压力和抑郁，显然尼古丁发挥了作用。

sentences.en: It's addictive.
sentences.zh: 它会让人上瘾。

sentences.en: We know that.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这一点。

sentences.en: Some people have called for tobacco companies to lower nicotine levels in cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 有些人呼吁烟草公司降低香烟中的尼古丁含量。

sentences.en: Do you think this could work in helping people stop smoking, or is there more of a behavioral component to smoking that will also need to be addressed to help people quit?
sentences.zh: 你认为这在帮助人们戒烟方面有效吗？还是说吸烟中存在更多需要解决的行为因素，才能帮助人们戒烟？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: The FDA has funded research examining the impact of lower nicotine cigarettes on smoking behavior and also toxin exposure.
sentences.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）资助了研究，考察低尼古丁香烟对吸烟行为以及毒素暴露的影响。

sentences.en: We know that women smoking is less motivated by nicotine and more influenced by what's called non-nicotine factors,
sentences.zh: 我们知道女性吸烟受尼古丁驱动的程度较低，更多地受到所谓的非尼古丁因素的影响，

sentences.en: such as sensory factors like the sight and the smell of a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 比如感官因素，如香烟的视觉和气味。

sentences.en: So in this work that's being funded by the FDA, it'll be critical to investigate whether women and men react differently to these lower nicotine cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 因此，在FDA资助的这项工作中，调查女性和男性对这些低尼古丁香烟的反应是否不同将至关重要。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: This has been very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有意思。

sentences.en: I appreciate you coming and talking with us, Dr. McKee.
sentences.zh: 我很感谢你能来和我们交谈，麦基博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: For more information on the 50th anniversary of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多关于美国卫生局局长关于吸烟与健康报告发布50周年的信息，以及麦基博士的研究，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: Surgeon General's report on smoking and health and Dr. McKee's work, please visit our website at speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的《心理学谈话》节目，

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology,
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton.
